 I couldn't cry when he died, but I don't know why. I thought he was just leaving. Like my Mum had, or like my best friend at the time, Matt. So I nodded and tried to say something, but realized that I had lost the ability to speak. I think I must have looked scared, because she put her hand on my shoulder and said, "It's okay, honey. We'll be taking care of your pain soon." I wasn't in pain. At least, I don't think so...I couldn't tell. Then I started to feel tired, and I realized that I was going to fall asleep in front of this woman. Not good! I've done embarrassing things before, but I don't want this to be one of them! I remember trying to stay awake as long as I could. My eyelids wouldn't cooperate, though, and before I knew it, I was out cold. I don't know how long I was there, but when I awoke, I found myself in an operating room, waiting for the procedure to begin. I watched the doctor come in, and noticed that he was holding a camera. He said something to the anesthesiologist, but I couldn't hear it. I felt the medication go into my body, and I felt myself slipping away again, this time for good. 
 
 The next time I woke up, I was in the dentist's office waiting room again. I could tell from the time displayed on the clock that it had only been a few seconds after the last time. It took me a few seconds to realize something. I knew I was sitting in my dentist's waiting room, but I wasn't in my body. The room was EXACTLY the same, but there was something off. It was like something out of a movie, when a character has been teleported into a different space.

I felt like I had been punched, and was stunned, for at least ten seconds, maybe longer. I grabbed my rifle and ran out the door and got into the Land Cruiser. The ground shuddered beneath me. I hit the ignition and backed down the alley, as another landing pod hit the ground in the next alley over. Once I was through the city gate, I looked at my GPS. It said we were only three miles from the center of town. 

I got into the Humvee with my team and we all grabbed our weapons. We checked our gear, checked all of our weapons. We were ready. We left the building and turned south. 

"We have 45 minutes to get to the center of town," I said. "If the Ssum have come in here, they've been pretty damned quiet about it. The buildings have been standing this whole time, so our guys have been hanging on them. We need to get to the center as soon as possible." 

The Humvees started up and we drove north. The streets were mostly clear as far as we could see. It looked like the Ssum had left the area, or had gotten bored with the attack. 

"I don't know, guys," I said. "Maybe they know that if we keep them here, they can't spread out and hit anyone else. But we can't just sit here. We have to move, somehow. And we can't fight our way out of this place. They're too well-armed and well-trained. We need to think of something." 

"We should try to make it to the main square," said one of my team members. "They'll have to come in that way. It's the only way to get to the center of town." 

"I agree," I said.

 `` I'm not even getting any credit for this,'' I mumbled. I don't know if he heard me. He started up the machine again. The lights started to blink, slowly getting brighter and brighter until the room was filled with the harsh light of a hundred computer monitors. The sensors were hooked up to my face and my torso, but as they were reading more data in the air, they were slowly taking up my limbs. My arms, my legs, my knees, my torso. Even my head. My head was the last to go. The sensors were connected to every inch of my body. They couldn't put me into the computer this time. They couldn't even give me an upgrade. 
 
 The computer came to life. I was inside my head and they were in front of me. I can't explain how they were there, but they were. They just stood there and watched, the monitor in front of them showing their reflection. I could feel myself turning and turning, until I was standing in front of them, still feeling like I'm standing on my head.
